source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
Identify all sources of income and expenses.
3. Separate operating losses from non-operating losses.
4. Use proper accounting principles to calculate losses.
5. Document each loss category clearly and separately (e.g., cost of goods sold, operating expenses, non-operating expenses, etc.).
6. Note any extraordinary items or one-time charges that affect revenues and expenses separately.
7. Reconcile the losses with bank statements and other financial evidence.
8. Document any inventory write-downs or adjustments due to obsolete inventory.
9. Clearly state any asset impairment losses, such as bad debts or property depreciation.
10. Describe the impact of any restructurings or discontinued operations.
11. Summarize totals for each loss category and provide a consolidated total loss for the period.
12. Ensure the disclosures comply with GAAP (Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) or IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) depending on the jurisdiction.
13. Explain any changes
